$meta.name: AgriLog v2 design tokens
$meta.sourceNote: This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: mobile/src/theme.ts and web-admin/src/app/tokens.css are generated from it by `node shared/design/build-tokens.js`. Never hard-code colours in components.
$meta.designNote: v6 keeps v5's flat, quiet system in the spirit of Stripe / Vercel / Apple (white or gray-50 grounds, hairline borders, one green primary, soft pastel badges, light shadows, an 8pt grid) and retunes it to the Phase 5 palette: the gray ramp moves from blue-tinted to neutral (#1A1A1A -> #F8F9FA), semantics become the Bootstrap set, and radii land on 6/8/12. See docs/adr/0004-he-thiet-ke-phang.md. The brand green (#2E6F40) is unchanged since v4.
$meta.v6Note: Three Phase 5 asks were deliberately NOT taken: button/input heights stay at 52/50 (the `size` block below is a field constraint, not taste), the font stays bundled Open Sans (the app must render identically offline), and body text stays 15px for sunlight readability. The one concession is `color.gradient`, used only as the login ground.
$meta.fontNote: Open Sans is BUNDLED with the app (mobile/src/assets/fonts, web-admin/public/fonts). Never load it from Google Fonts at runtime - the farmer app must work offline.

gray.$note: v6 neutral ramp. The keys are unchanged from v5 so no component has to be touched; only the hues move off the blue tint. 50/100 are the two page grounds, 200/300 the two border weights, 400 placeholder, 500 caption, 700 body, 900 heading.

semantic.$note: Status colours for text/icons/borders - never as a full-bleed fill. Pair them with the soft `badge` pairs below when a surface is needed.

accent.$note: v6.2 (mobile Phase 1). Used ONLY to colour an icon tile apart from its neighbours so a wall of green gains a second and third note - never for text (neither clears AA on white) and never as a page ground.

gradient.$note: The ground tint behind the farmer-facing screens. v6.2 warms the far end from gray-100 to the soft green so the ground belongs to the brand instead of reading as plain gray; the two stops are still close enough to read as a tint, not a gradient. Mobile renders it as interpolated bands (no native gradient dependency - react-native-linear-gradient was removed in v5). No web-admin rule consumes these, so the change stops at the phone.

badge.$note: Soft pastel pairs only - never a saturated fill. yellow = warning / missing data, green = ok / popular, red = danger / low stock, gray = neutral, blue = new / info, purple = premium.

banner.$note: Full-bleed status line above every screen - saturated on purpose, unlike the badge pastels, because losing signal has to read at a glance in sunlight.

shadow.$note: All light - nothing darker than these anywhere in the app. sm/md/lg are the original scale and are what web-admin's CSS consumes, so their values are frozen. card/raised/brand are the softer, wider v6.2 set the phone uses; they are additive precisely so the phone can get rounder and airier without moving a pixel on the web.

radius.$note: xs = 6, sm = 8, md = 12 (buttons, inputs), lg = 16, xl = 24, pill = badges. `card` is the v6.2 mobile card corner; sm/md/lg stay put because web-admin's CSS reads them.

space.$note: 8pt grid. xs/md are the two half-steps the grid allows for tight inner spacing.

size.$note: Field constraints - hard minimums for muddy hands and sunlight. They outrank aesthetics.
